description: Compatibility traps, inherited build to build so they are recorded rather than rediscovered (REQ-VER-05). A20 applies every rule here after reading the registries and before finalising versions/manifest.json. A trap is never deleted on a hunch - it is superseded with a reason.

traps.rule: Pin the major to the current Node LTS major, not to the registry's latest.
traps.why: npm 'latest' for @types/node tracks the newest Node major, which may be a release line we do not run (REQ-VER-06 puts us on the LTS). Bumping it to match npm latest is a regression, not an upgrade.

traps.rule: Do not adopt the 7.x line until the pinned next, @biomejs/biome and drizzle-kit versions are externally confirmed to support it. Record the outcome either way.
traps.why: TypeScript 7 is the native rewrite, not an incremental major. Tooling support lags a rewrite, and REQ-VER-04 makes a major jump a reviewed decision with a migration note.
traps.action: Write versions/notes/typescript-7.md and get human acknowledgement, or pin the newest 5.x line with the reason recorded.

traps.rule: Verify RFC 5424 structured-data emission and RFC 5425 TLS transport against the actual package before adopting it.
traps.why: Low release activity, and REQ-AUD-07 plus REQ-SEC-05 require both. A package that cannot do TLS transport fails the security gate, and discovering that after A13 has built against it costs a round.
traps.action: If it cannot do TLS transport, frame RFC 5424 directly over a tls.TLSSocket and record the decision.

traps.rule: Invoke via npx/pnpm dlx. Never add it to dependencies, and never hand-decode a preset code - use `npx shadcn@latest preset decode <code>`.
traps.why: It is a scaffolding CLI. A hand-decoded preset silently produces a different theme than the one the requirement names (REQ-UI-04).

traps.rule: Major 9. Do not carry v8 patterns across; check the current API before writing row-model code.
traps.why: Most published examples and training-era knowledge are v8. REQ-GRD-01 puts the whole grid on this package, so a v8 assumption propagates into twelve surfaces.
